issues.legal_issue: A descendant born after intestate devolution of a deceased coparcener’s interest cannot claim a birthright or maintain a partition suit in property that has ceased to be joint family property.
material_facts: The property was ancestral Mitakshara coparcenary property, and no earlier partition among the coparceners had taken place.

The grandfather died leaving a widow who was a Class I heir. Under the law then applicable, a partition was deemed to occur immediately before his death, and his interest devolved by intestate succession.
The claimant was born after the grandfather’s death and later sued for partition during his father’s lifetime, claiming a share by birth.
Following the succession, the heirs held the property as tenants in common, rather than as joint tenants.
issues.conclusion: The property ceased to be joint family property when the grandfather’s interest devolved by succession. Since the claimant was born afterward, he acquired no birthright in it, and his partition suit was not maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4, 6 (before its 2005 amendment), 8 and 19 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, where the proviso to old Section 6 applies, the deceased coparcener’s interest devolves by testamentary or intestate succession rather than survivorship. Explanation 1 to old Section 6 requires a deemed partition immediately before death to determine that interest. Once the property devolves under Section 8, the heirs take as tenants in common under Section 19, and the property ceases to be joint family property. Section 30 permits testamentary disposition of a coparcenary interest. The Court applied G.K. Magdum v. H.K. Magdum, (1978) 3 SCR 761, and Shyama Devi v. Manju Shukla, (1994) 6 SCC 342, on the deemed partition; Commissioner of Wealth Tax v. Chander Sen, (1986) 3 SCC 567, Yudhishter v. Ashok Kumar, (1987) 1 SCC 204, and Bhanwar Singh v. Puran, (2008) 3 SCC 87, on devolution under Section 8 and the resulting status of the property. It distinguished State of Maharashtra v. Narayan Rao Sham Rao Deshmukh, (1985) 3 SCR 358, and held that the cases concerning property continuing as joint family property with a sole surviving coparcener did not alter the result because they did not consider the effect of Sections 4, 8 and 19.

rule.if: partition_suit and property_was_mitakshara_coparcenary and deceased_left_class_i_female_heir and deceased_interest_devolved_by_intestacy and claimant_born_after_devolution

predicates.partition_suit: A claimant brought a proceeding seeking partition of property.
predicates.property_was_mitakshara_coparcenary: The property was held as Mitakshara coparcenary property before the relevant death.
predicates.deceased_left_class_i_female_heir: The deceased coparcener was survived by a female heir in the first class of heirs.
predicates.deceased_interest_devolved_by_intestacy: The deceased coparcener’s interest passed to heirs by intestate succession rather than survivorship.
predicates.claimant_born_after_devolution: The claimant was born after the deceased coparcener’s interest had devolved to the heirs.

issues.definition: When a partition suit concerns former Mitakshara coparcenary property and the stated succession and birth facts apply, the claimant cannot maintain the suit as a birthright holder.

issues.legal_issue: The 2005 amendment to the law governing devolution of coparcenary interests does not affect a partition completed by court decree before the amendment’s protected cutoff.
material_facts: The partition suit was filed in 1998 and a decree was made in 2000.
The 2005 amendment commenced after the decree, and its saving provision protected partitions completed by court decree before the specified cutoff.
issues.conclusion: The 2005 amendment did not affect the decree in this case and did not govern the parties’ rights.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 6 as amended in 2005 preserves dispositions, alienations, partitions and testamentary dispositions completed before 20 December 2004; the explanation recognizes a partition effected by a court decree. The amendment commenced on 9 September 2005. Because the decree here preceded the protected cutoff, it was not affected by the amendment.

predicates.appeal_concerning_partition_rights: A party appealed in a proceeding concerning rights to partition property.
predicates.partition_completed_by_court_decree_befo: A court completed the partition by decree before the applicable preservation cutoff.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning partition rights, a partition completed by court decree before the protected cutoff is not affected by the 2005 amendment.
